name: International Cryptozoology Museum
summary: Loren Coleman's famous collection of cryptid casts, replicas and pop-culture oddities. After years at Thompson's Point in Portland it has been moving into a larger home on Broadway in Bangor.
price: $10 adults, $5 kids 12 and under (last posted rates)
note: Mid-move from Portland to Bangor. Check the museum site for the opening date before you go.

name: Mothman Museum
address: 400 Main Street, Point Pleasant, West Virginia
summary: The world's only museum devoted to the red-eyed Mothman, with witness accounts, news clippings from 1966 and 1967 and a pile of Mothman memorabilia. It sits a few steps from the steel Mothman statue and runs tours of the TNT area.

name: North American Bigfoot Center
summary: Cliff Barackman of TV's Finding Bigfoot runs this museum near Mount Hood, packed with footprint casts, field gear and a walk-through history of Sasquatch research.

name: Expedition: Bigfoot! The Sasquatch Museum
summary: A roadside museum in the north Georgia mountains packed with Bigfoot figures, track casts and sighting reports. The self-guided walk takes about an hour.
price: $8 to $9 adults, $6 kids 5 to 12, under 5 free

name: Flatwoods Monster Museum
summary: Braxton County's visitor centre doubles as a shrine to the 1952 Flatwoods Monster, with early sketches, an original 'Home of the Green Monster' sign and plenty of merch.

name: West Virginia Bigfoot Museum
summary: A small family-run museum a few blocks from the Flatwoods Monster Museum, with local footprint casts, a full-size Bigfoot figure and a binder of West Virginia sightings.

name: Skunk Ape Research Headquarters
summary: Everglades roadside stop dedicated to Florida's smelly swamp ape, with a gift shop, Skunk Ape lore and a back area of live reptiles and birds.
price: Admission charged for the animal area and tours

name: International UFO Museum and Research Center
address: 114 North Main Street, Roswell, New Mexico
summary: Roswell's main attraction tells the 1947 crash story with documents, timelines, alien dioramas and a big research library.

name: Willow Creek-China Flat Museum (Bigfoot Collection)
summary: A local history museum in the self-styled Bigfoot Capital of the World, with a whole Bigfoot wing of track casts, photos and newspaper clippings.
note: Seasonal hours, mostly spring to fall.

name: Harrison Visitor Centre and Sasquatch Museum
address: 499 Hot Springs Road, Harrison Hot Springs, British Columbia
summary: Free museum in the village where the word Sasquatch was born, from the Sts'ailes Sa:sq'ets. Casts, carvings, a longhouse room and an 8-foot statue for photos.

name: Shag Harbour UFO Centre
summary: A small seasonal museum on the shore where, in October 1967, witnesses reported a lit object dropping into the sea and the RCMP and navy went looking.
note: Open in summer, roughly June to September.

name: Bigfoot Crossroads of America
summary: Harriett McFeely, the "Bigfoot Lady", opened this three-building museum in 2018 with skulls, casts and a sightings map that includes Nebraska reports.

name: Cryptozoology and Paranormal Museum
address: 300 North Main Street, Littleton, North Carolina
summary: Former mayor Stephen Barcelo fills this small-town museum with an 8-foot Bigfoot, track casts, UFO material, a haunted doll and a shelf of famous fakes.

name: Fouke Monster Mart
summary: A convenience store with a mini museum of Boggy Creek clippings, track casts and Legend of Boggy Creek photos, plus a big monster statue out front.

name: Sasquatch Outpost
summary: A Bigfoot gift shop with a museum out back: track casts, a pinned map of trusted Colorado sightings and the infamous "Tremendous Turd".

name: Pine Bush UFO and Paranormal Museum
address: 86 Main Street, Pine Bush, New York
summary: The Hudson Valley's UFO town opened this museum in 2021 to tell the story of the area's many sightings, with exhibits on lights, crafts and the paranormal.

name: South Carolina Cotton Museum (Lizard Man exhibit)
summary: The town museum in the old train depot keeps a Lizard Man exhibit with plaster casts from the 1988 Scape Ore Swamp sighting and a sign from the original site.

name: Paranormal Museum
address: Cookman Avenue, Asbury Park, New Jersey
summary: Kathy Kelly runs this Cookman Avenue museum of the strange and hosts the yearly Jersey Devil Festival on the street behind it.

name: The Loch Ness Centre
summary: Themed rooms walk you through the story of Loch Ness, its famous sightings and its hoaxes, and you can add a sonar cruise on the loch itself.

name: Jamtli: Great Lake Monster exhibit
summary: Sweden's Storsjön lake monster gets its own exhibit at the Jamtli museum: slide in through the creature's belly, hear witness tapes and see a 19th-century monster trap.

name: Mothman Festival
summary: Huge crowds fill downtown Point Pleasant for speakers, vendors, food trucks, live music and hayrides. It is the biggest cryptid party in the country.

name: Rougarou Fest
summary: A free, family Halloween-season festival in Cajun country honouring the swamp werewolf, with costumes, music, food and local culture.

name: Kelly Little Green Men Days
summary: The tiny town of Kelly marks the August 1955 night a farm family said small glowing creatures besieged their house, with rides, music and alien souvenirs.
when: Mid to late August, near the August 21 anniversary
note: We could not find a Little Green Men Days since 2023. GoblinCon in nearby Hopkinsville now marks the anniversary each August.

name: WNC Bigfoot Festival
summary: Downtown Marion goes Bigfoot-crazy for a day of speakers, a calling contest, vendors and a 5K, with free shuttles from parking.

name: Roswell UFO Festival
summary: Roswell celebrates the 1947 crash every Fourth of July weekend with a costume parade, drone show, the Alien Chase run and speakers at the UFO Museum.

name: McMenamins UFO Festival
summary: Born from the famous 1950 Trent farm saucer photos, this long-running festival brings speakers, an alien costume parade and a lot of beer to McMenamins Hotel Oregon.

name: Fouke Monster (Boggy Creek) Festival
summary: A spring weekend of talks, vendors and bus tours of Boggy Creek country in the town that inspired The Legend of Boggy Creek.
when: Spring, most often March or April

name: Frogman Festival
summary: A cryptid art and makers convention honouring the Loveland Frogman, with costumed frogs, a parade, puppet shows and live reptiles.

name: Smoky Mountain Bigfoot Festival
summary: A Bigfoot "birthday bash" on the quiet side of the Smokies with a 5K and fun run, vendors and family activities.

name: Smoky Mountain Bigfoot Conference
summary: A one-day conference in Gatlinburg with well-known researchers and TV names. Tickets sell in advance.

name: Ohio Bigfoot Conference
summary: One of the longest-running Bigfoot gatherings, held every spring since 2005 at the lodge in Salt Fork State Park, a sighting hotspot.

name: Hocking Hills Bigfoot Festival
summary: A multi-day summer festival with speakers, vendors and family fun. It moved to the Vinton County Fairgrounds in 2025.

name: Marfa Lights Festival
summary: West Texas toasts its mystery lights with a parade, street dances, food and music over Labor Day weekend. Most of it is free.

name: Bigfoot Daze
summary: The Bigfoot Capital's hometown party, running for more than 60 years, with a parade and small-town fun. It moved from Labor Day to late June in 2026.

name: Kecksburg UFO Festival
summary: The volunteer fire company celebrates the 1965 "acorn" crash with a parade, food trucks and vendors, all to fund the fire hall where the acorn replica lives.

name: Exeter UFO Festival
summary: Marks the 1965 Incident at Exeter with a speaker series, kids' activities and trolley rides. The Kiwanis Club runs it and gives the profits to local charities.

name: Texas Bigfoot Conference
summary: The original Texas Bigfoot conference, run since 2001 in a historic Piney Woods town, with big-name speakers and vendors.

name: Belleville UFO Days
summary: A village parade, games and alien costumes in Library Park, started after a 1987 police sighting of a strange object over town.
when: Usually the last Saturday of October

name: Elmwood UFO Days
summary: The self-declared UFO Capital of Wisconsin has thrown this summer festival since 1978, with sighting bus tours, speakers, tractor pulls and an alien parade.

name: Pine Bush UFO Fair
summary: A free Main Street fair with alien cosplay, paranormal talks, live music and a "Best in Galaxy" costume pageant.

name: Contact in the Desert
summary: Billed as the biggest UFO conference around: five days of talks, workshops and night sky watches in the Coachella Valley.

name: Sasquatch Days
summary: Co-hosted by the village and the Sts'ailes Nation, with war canoe races, cultural programs and Sasquatch talks on Harrison Lake.

name: West Virginia Bigfoot Festival
address: 19 Memorial Park Road, Summersville, West Virginia
summary: Hosted by the West Virginia Bigfoot Museum. After years in Sutton it moved to Veterans Memorial Park in Summersville for 2026.
when: Moved from June to October in 2026

name: Remer Bigfoot Days
summary: The self-proclaimed Home of Bigfoot throws a two-day party with storytelling, Bigfoot Olympics, a 5K, a calling contest and BBQ.

name: Shag Harbour UFO Expo
summary: Three days of talks near the anniversary of the 1967 Shag Harbour incident, with a bus tour to the crash area and the old CFB Shelburne site.
note: The 2026 expo was cancelled after the death of Shag Harbour Incident Society president Laurie Wickens. The society is pointing to the 60th anniversary in 2027; no dates yet.

name: Manipogo Festival
summary: St. Laurent on Lake Manitoba celebrates Manipogo, the humped lake monster named in 1960, with a winter festival.

name: Forest County Bigfoot Festival
summary: A three-day June festival in the Allegheny National Forest with 160-plus vendors, TV guests and a famous 5-mile Bigfoot hunt.

name: Bigfoot on 66 Festival
summary: A free afternoon of Bigfoot art and folklore on Route 66, with a calling contest, workshops and a scavenger hunt.

name: Metaline Falls Bigfoot Festival
summary: A small-town June weekend for Sasquatch fans in Busta Park, in Washington's far northeast corner.

name: Squatch Watch Vancouver Island
summary: A three-day Sasquatch conference in the Comox Valley with presenters, a vendor market and a gala dinner, partnered with the Queneesh Indigenous Community Society.

name: Jersey Devil Fable Fest
summary: Cookman Avenue closes for costumed cryptids, storytellers, spooky vendors and a film festival honouring New Jersey's famous devil.
note: This replaced the shop's older Jersey Devil Festival.

name: Mothman Statue
address: 4th Street and Main Street, Point Pleasant, West Virginia
summary: Bob Roach's gleaming stainless-steel Mothman, about 12 feet tall with spread wings and red eyes, has stood downtown since 2003. Everyone takes the photo.

name: The TNT Area (McClintic Wildlife Management Area)
summary: Old WWII explosives works north of town, still dotted with concrete igloos, where four young people first reported Mothman on November 15, 1966.
note: Public wildlife land. Stay out of the bunkers.

name: Flatwoods Monster Chair Trail
summary: Five 10-foot chairs shaped like the 1952 monster are spread from Flatwoods through Sutton to Gassaway. Photograph all five for a "Free Braxxie" sticker.

name: Marfa Lights Viewing Area
summary: A roadside pavilion 9 miles east of Marfa on US 90, built for watching the mystery lights that bob over the desert some nights.
note: Come after dark. The lights do not show every night.

name: Ogopogo Statue
summary: Kelowna's most photographed public art: a fibreglass Ogopogo on the downtown waterfront, sculpted in 1960.

name: Champ Sightings Board
address: South Main Street, Port Henry, New York
summary: A big roadside board on Bulwagga Bay listing over 130 reported Champ sightings in Lake Champlain. Port Henry also throws a summer Champ Day.

name: The Bigfoot Trap
summary: A big box trap built in 1974 to catch a Sasquatch. It only ever caught bears and now sits open on the Collings Mountain Trail.
note: Short hike from Hart-tish Park on Applegate Lake.

name: UFO Watchtower
summary: A viewing platform and quirky garden in the San Luis Valley, with campsites for overnight sky watching.

name: Little A'Le'Inn
summary: The only motel, bar and cafe on this stretch of the Extraterrestrial Highway near Area 51. Order the Alien Burger.

name: Alien Research Center
summary: A Quonset-hut gift shop at the start of the Extraterrestrial Highway, guarded by a giant silver alien.

name: UFO Landing Pad
summary: The world's first UFO landing pad, built in 1967 for Canada's centennial, sits on a time capsule due to open in 2067. A small UFO exhibit is next door.
note: Visitor centre open late May to early September.

name: Aurora Cemetery "Alien Grave"
summary: A Texas historical marker here notes the 1897 story of an airship crash and a pilot "not of this world" said to be buried in the cemetery.
note: Be respectful: it is a working cemetery.

name: Betty and Barney Hill Marker
summary: State historical marker on Route 3 for the 1961 Hill abduction story, the case that made "alien abduction" a household phrase.

name: Brown Mountain Lights Overlook
summary: Pull-off on NC 181 north of Morganton facing Brown Mountain, where glowing orbs have been reported for over a century.
note: Wiseman's View in Linville Gorge is the darker, harder-to-reach alternative.

name: The Integratron
summary: A wooden dome George Van Tassel began in the 1950s after messages he said came from Venusians. Today it hosts booked sound baths.

name: Bigfoot Scenic Byway
summary: California Highway 96 along the Klamath River from Willow Creek to Happy Camp, promoted as the region with the most Bigfoot sightings anywhere.

name: Ape Canyon
summary: Gorge on Mount St. Helens named for a 1924 story of miners besieged by rock-throwing 'apemen'. A popular trail runs alongside it.

name: Kilcoy Yowie Statue
summary: The self-styled Yowie capital of Australia put a big Yowie statue in Yowie Park after a famous 1979 sighting nearby.

name: Murray Bridge Bunyip
address: Sturt Reserve, Murray Bridge, South Australia
summary: Press the button at Sturt Reserve and a roaring animatronic Bunyip rises from its riverside cave. It has been scaring kids since 1972.

name: Rendlesham Forest UFO Trail
summary: A 3-mile waymarked walk past the spots linked to Britain's most famous UFO case, the December 1980 lights near the RAF/USAF bases.
note: Sections close for timber work. Check Forestry England before you go.

name: Remer, "Home of Bigfoot"
summary: A Chippewa National Forest town that leaned into Bigfoot after a 2009 trail-camera video, with Bigfoot cutouts, casts and a statue at the gas station.

name: Issie Statue, Lake Ikeda
summary: Japan's answer to Nessie. A statue of Issie stands on the shore of Kyushu's largest caldera lake, where sightings peaked in 1978.

name: Khumjung Monastery Yeti Scalp
summary: A conical "yeti scalp" kept in a glass case at this Everest-region monastery. Hillary borrowed it for testing in 1960. A side trip on the Base Camp trek.
note: Reachable on foot only.

name: Varginha UFO Water Tower and ET Memorial
summary: The Brazilian city of the 1996 "ET of Varginha" built a flying-saucer water tower and an ET memorial, reopened in 2024.

name: Mawnan Church (Owlman)
summary: A clifftop church in Cornwall where two sisters said they saw a man-sized owl with red eyes over the tower in 1976.

name: World's Largest Hodag
summary: Rhinelander's horned, grinning Hodag, a lumberjack hoax from 1893, guards the visitor centre. Lit at night.

name: Ponik Sculpture
summary: Quebec's lake monster Ponik, reported since 1874, is honoured with a huge sculpture at the lakeside resort.

name: Lake Pepin (Pepie)
summary: Lake City says a serpent called Pepie lives in this wide stretch of the Mississippi and offers $50,000 for proof.

name: Aztec UFO Crash Site
summary: A plaque on a mesa trail marks the claimed 1948 saucer crash in Hart Canyon. The story is widely called a hoax, but the hike is lovely.

name: Alleged UFO Skip Site
summary: BLM land near Corona tied to the 1947 Roswell debris story. It is hike-in only, and the BLM sometimes leads guided walks.

name: Jackalope Statue
summary: Douglas, where taxidermists invented the antlered rabbit in the 1930s, has a big jackalope statue downtown and more around town.

name: Sasquatch Provincial Park
summary: Lakes, trails and campgrounds just north of Harrison Hot Springs, renamed for the Sasquatch in 1968.

name: Kecksburg Acorn
summary: The acorn-shaped replica made for Unsolved Mysteries, modelled on the object witnesses said fell in 1965, now sits at the Kecksburg fire hall.

name: North Fork Survivors Bigfoot
summary: A towering concrete Bigfoot beside a gift shop and an A-frame half-buried by the 1980 Mount St. Helens mudflow.
note: Shop hours vary. Call ahead.

name: UFO McDonald's
address: 720 North Main Street, Roswell, New Mexico
summary: A McDonald's built in flying-saucer style with glowing trim and a space-themed play area. Only in Roswell.

name: Alien Fresh Jerky
summary: An alien-themed jerky store on the way to Vegas, with spaceship props and flavours like Abducted Cow Teriyaki.

name: Cerro Uritorco
summary: Argentina's UFO mountain. Up to 200,000 people a year climb it, and the town below has a UFO information centre.

name: The Sea Serpent (Igopogo)
summary: Barrie's waterfront sculpture of Igopogo, aka Kempenfelt Kelly, the Lake Simcoe monster reported since the 1800s.

name: Memphré Sculpture
summary: A sculpture of Memphré, the Lake Memphremagog monster, in the lakeside Parc de la Baie-de-Magog.

name: Falcon Lake Incident Site
summary: In May 1967 prospector Stefan Michalak said a landed craft burned his chest here. Parks Manitoba has run anniversary hikes to the site.

name: Mothman Museum TNT Area Tours
summary: Guided tours of the TNT area where Mothman was first seen, sold through the Mothman Museum. They sell out early in spring.

name: Area 51 Day Tour (Adventure Photo Tours)
summary: A 10-hour trip from Las Vegas in a small 4x4 to the edge of the Area 51 restricted zone, with a driver-guide, lunch and snacks included.

name: Sedona UFO Night-Vision Tours
summary: Several Sedona outfits take small groups into dark desert with military-grade night-vision goggles to scan for satellites, meteors and whatever else is up there.

name: Loch Ness Deepscan Cruise
summary: A sonar-equipped boat trip on Loch Ness from the Loch Ness Centre, with a combined cruise and exhibition ticket available.

name: Honey Island Swamp Boat Tours
summary: Two-hour boat trips into the swamp the Honey Island Swamp Monster is said to haunt. You will definitely see gators.

name: Salt Fork Bigfoot Night Hikes
summary: The park naturalist leads seasonal after-dark Bigfoot hikes in Salt Fork State Park, one of Ohio's busiest sighting areas.
note: Monthly in season. Watch the park Facebook page for dates.

name: Out the Top Adventures Bigfoot Hunt
summary: A night ride in a side-by-side to a scouted spot in the Red River Gorge area, then a guided deep-woods Bigfoot hunt.

name: Rabbit Hole Adventures
summary: Colorado outfitter offering Bigfoot night hikes and multi-day camping searches in Park County.
price: About $125 night hike, $650 for three days

name: Adirondack Bigfoot Cruise
address: Steel Pier, Lake George, New York
summary: An evening sail on the Minne Ha Ha steam paddlewheeler with Bigfoot researchers and a Q&A.

name: Dobhar-chú Headstone, Conwal Cemetery
summary: An old headstone in Conwal (Congbháil) Cemetery in the Glenade valley is carved with the Dobhar-chú, the 'water hound' said to have killed a local woman at Glenade Lough. Tradition says it marks her grave.
note: Location approximate: the cemetery is in the Glenade valley north of Manorhamilton.

name: Holy Trinity Church, Blythburgh (Black Shuck)
summary: On 4 August 1577, during a violent storm, the black dog Black Shuck is said to have burst into this church and attacked the congregation, after killing two people at Bungay church 12 miles away the same morning. Scorch-like marks on the north door are still linked to the legend.

name: Peel Castle (Moddey Dhoo)
summary: The ruined castle on St Patrick's Isle is the haunt of the Moddey Dhoo, a spectral black dog. In the legend, a soldier who went alone to face it came back speechless and died a few days later.

name: Musée Fantastique de la Bête du Gévaudan
summary: In the heart of the country where the Beast killed dozens of people between 1764 and 1767, this museum retells the story in 24 scenes, from the first attacks to the royal hunts.
note: Location approximate: the museum is in Saugues town centre.

name: Kappabuchi Pool
summary: A quiet stream pool behind a temple in Tōno, the town of Japan's famous folk legends, where kappa are said to live. It's one of the town's best-known sights for anyone tracing the old stories.
note: Location approximate: the pool is in the Tsuchibuchi district of Tōno.

name: National Leprechaun Museum
summary: A storytelling museum on Jervis Street devoted to Irish folklore, from leprechauns and fairy forts to banshees and changelings, told in guided tours and evening dark-side shows.

name: Crescent Lake (Cressie)
summary: The town of Roberts Arm proudly claims Cressie, the eel-like monster of Crescent Lake. A hiking trail runs along the end of the lake nearest town, a good spot to watch the water.
note: Location is the town; the lake is just beside it.

name: Lake Seljord (Selma)
summary: The 13 km lake in Telemark is home to Selma, the Seljord serpent of Norwegian folklore, and the lake has been searched by monster-hunting expeditions. The village makes the most of its serpent.

name: Hessdalen Valley
summary: A 15 km valley in central Norway famous for unexplained balls of light, especially during a wave of sightings in the early 1980s. An automatic measurement station has watched the sky here since 1998.

name: Champ Day
summary: A one-day lakeside festival honouring Champ, the Lake Champlain monster, run by the Moriah Chamber of Commerce since the 1980s.
when: A Saturday in late July or early August

name: Bigfoot Days
summary: A free Saturday festival in Bond Park with talks, a Bigfoot calling contest, races and vendors, plus a ticketed Friday BBQ.

name: Upper Cumberland Bigfoot Festival
summary: A charity festival at the Cumberland County Community Complex raising money for local veterans, with TV guests, vendors and wrestling.

name: Flatwoods Monster Convention
summary: A small convention near Flatwoods marking the 1952 Flatwoods Monster sighting, with speakers, vendors and a costume contest.

name: Lizard Man Stomp
summary: A downtown street festival honouring the 1988 Lizard Man of Scape Ore Swamp, with a parade, car show, food trucks and music.

name: Tsuchinoko Festa
summary: A village festival where families search the hills for the tsuchinoko, a legendary fat-bodied snake, with a cash prize for proof.

name: Van Meter Visitor Festival
summary: A one-day festival about the 1903 winged Van Meter Visitor, with guided monster walking tours and paranormal talks.

name: Festival Alienígena
summary: A free town festival near Cerro Uritorco with a costume parade, ufology talks, music and astro-tourism; 2026 was the 10th edition.
when: About ten days in early to mid February

name: Australian UFO Festival
summary: Australia's only dedicated UFO festival (formerly the Cardwell UFO Festival, since 2014), with forum talks, a market day and an alien party.
when: Early August (long weekend, Thursday/Friday to Sunday)

name: sQuatch Fest + Galactic Fest
summary: A winter weekend at the Cowlitz County Event Center pairing Bigfoot and UFO talks with vendors, craft ales and kids' activities.

name: Fyffe UFO Days
summary: A free town park festival recalling the 1989 Fyffe sightings, with balloon rides, music, a car and tractor show and a 5K.

name: Seriously Strange Conference (ASSAP)
summary: The Association for the Scientific Study of Anomalous Phenomena's annual conference on ghosts, UFOs and other anomalies; 2026 marked its 45th year.
when: Annual weekend, usually late summer (venue varies)
note: The conference moves to a different town each year. Worcester hosted in 2026.

name: Iino UFO Festival
summary: A festival in Iino-machi, a UFO-lore town near Mount Senganmori, built around an alien costume parade and contest of about 2,000 people.

name: Honobia Bigfoot Festival & Conference
summary: A two-day festival at the Kiamichi Mountains Christian Mission with a Bigfoot conference, story night, vendors and a 5K.

name: Beast Fest
summary: A downtown festival honouring the 1954 Beast of Bladenboro, with bands, a car show and costume contests.

name: Sasquatch Summit
summary: A research conference at the Quinault Beach Resort and Casino with speakers, panels and vendors.
when: A weekend in mid to late November

name: Great Florida Bigfoot Conference
summary: A conference at the World Equestrian Center with Bigfoot and Skunk Ape speakers, vendors and town halls; 2026 was the 6th.

name: Bell Witch Fall Festival
summary: A month of outdoor theatre and storytelling at the old Bell School about the Bell Witch haunting of the 1810s.

name: Spruce Pine Alien Festival
summary: A free downtown festival with UFO speakers, a costume contest, 100-plus vendors and music.

name: Sasquatch Summer Fest
summary: A summer festival in the Willamette National Forest town of Oakridge celebrating Sasquatch over two days.

name: Whitehall Sasquatch Festival & Calling Contest
summary: A free festival in a Champlain Valley town known for 1970s Bigfoot reports, with a calling contest, beer garden and researchers.

name: Central PA Bigfoot & Cryptid Festival
summary: A free one-day festival of speakers and vendors, started in Elysburg and now held at the Susquehanna Valley Mall.
when: A Saturday in early to mid August

name: Cryptids and Paranormal Conference
summary: A one-day conference at the Crowne Plaza Princeton covering Bigfoot, other cryptids and the paranormal; 2026 was the 4th.

name: Uwharrie Bigfoot Festival
summary: A three-day festival in the Uwharrie region with researchers, a call contest, music and an NC Bronco show; 2026 was its second year.

name: KC Cryptid Con
summary: An adults-only one-day cryptid conference run by the Oz Paranormal Institute covering Sasquatch, Dogman and Mothman.

name: Carolina CryptidFest
summary: A two-day cryptid fair at the NC State Fairgrounds' Jim Graham Building with vendors, speakers and live music.

name: GoblinCon UFO and Paranormal Expo
summary: A two-day expo at the James E. Bruce Convention Center marking the 1955 Kelly-Hopkinsville goblin encounter, with 70-plus vendors and talks.
when: Around the Aug 21 anniversary of the 1955 encounter (2025 edition was in October)
note: Kelly's own Little Green Men Days has not been held since 2023, as far as we can find. GoblinCon now marks the 1955 encounter.
Whitey talks aren't on a fixed schedule. Check with the park before you go if you want one.
name: White River Monster Refuge (Jacksonport State Park)
summary: In 1973 Arkansas lawmakers made this stretch of the White River a legal refuge for Whitey, and it's against the law to harm him inside it. The state's tourism listings name Jacksonport State Park as the refuge's home, and park interpreters have run Whitey talks here.

name: Rougarou Historic Marker
summary: A roadside marker put up in 2025, in English on one side and French on the other, calling the rougarou a werewolf-like creature of Cajun and French folklore believed to prowl the swamps of Terrebonne Parish.

note: Most of the swamp is private land. Look from the public roads and don't go wandering in.
name: Scape Ore Swamp
summary: The swamp outside Bishopville where 17-year-old Christopher Davis said a seven-foot green creature attacked his car while he changed a flat tire one night in 1988. Most Lizard Man reports since have come from around here.
